messages:
jen: Quick note  noticed the /v1/rerank API docs show each item as { score: 0.87 } but runtime emits `rank_score` in the JSON. This breaks the JS SDK example which expects `score`.

jen: Current docs snippet:```json
{"candidates": [{"id":"a","score":0.87},{"id":"b","score":0.12}]}
```

jen: Actual service response:```json
{"candidates": [{"id":"a","rank_score":0.87},{"id":"b","rank_score":0.12}]}
```

riley: Thanks, that's a good catch. We renamed the field upstream to avoid collisions with internal score semantics. Docs should reflect `rank_score` and SDKs should map to `score` for backwards compatibility.

jen: I'll open a docs PR to change examples + add a small compatibility note and a sample mapping in the JS snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/12725

riley: For JS snippet, recommend doing this mapping:```js
// server receives candidate objects with rank_score
const mapped = resp.candidates.map(c => ({ ...c, score: c.rank_score ?? c.score }));
```

jen: Adding that. Also adding a migration note: "Field note: `rank_score` replaces `score` in service responses; client libraries expose `score` for backward compatibility."

ci-bot: docs lint OK. staging build: https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/api/rerank (sha: d4e5f6).

jen: Preview looks good, updated examples render correctly. Assigning follow-ups: riley -> add changelog entry for runtime change, jen -> merge docs PR and notify Support. Closing after merge. :white_check_mark:
